title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Find Your Unfair Advantages*

Get to know yourself better and find your unique talent/skills, e.g., out of box thinker? strong analytic skills? fast coder? good communicator?

👉 Invest and grow your unfair advantages.

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Fundamentals*

Don't be distracted by all the fancy latest advances in your field. Spend time studying the fundamentals. Volunteer to TA for relevant courses! Teaching is the best way to learn.

👉 Getting a solid understanding of the fundamentals goes a long way!

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Course Grade*

Optimal GPA = Minimum required GPA + ε

Nobody cares about your course grade! 

It's okay to get an A. But, if you are getting an A+, something is wrong ... you should spend more time on your research.

👉 PhD is about producing new knowledge!

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Learn to Communicate Well*

Yep, it's important to learn all the technical skills. But it's equally important to learn how to communicate well. 

👉 Seize every opportunity to practice your writing and presentation skills (in every message, reading group talk).

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Attend Seminars*

Don't just attend talks on closely related topics about your work. Talks that are seemly irrelevant can broaden your horizons and bring you new insights! 

Plus, those free cookies are very tasty!

👉 You can always learn something from good (and bad) talks!

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
*Show Your Work*

A PhD is a lonely journey. Set up your personal website, a blog, a Twitter account and start sharing your work *in public*. Yes, it's scary, but your experiences will help others and attract people with similar interests.

👉 Find your peer support group!

title: How to survive the first year of PhD?
en:
Hope this is helpful! 

I for one cannot wait to see the amazing work many of you will be doing! 🤩

How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?

Congrats! 🎉 This is exciting! Your application stands out, and you are now on a shortlist of candidates. 

But, how do you nail the phone interview and move on to the next stage? 

Some tips👇

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
*Anticipate the questions*

The faculty search committee must ask all the candidates the same questions. This means that the interview questions are entirely PREDICTABLE, e.g., 

❓ why X (university/department)
❓ your future research agenda
❓ external funding plan
❓ courses to teach

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
*Practice your responses*

If you are not a native speaker or can speak fluently, practice, practice, practice. 

My recommendation: Write down your complete response and read it out loud many many times.

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
*Don’t just say, articulate*

As non-native speakers, our responses usually fall flat without all the expressive intonation. Practice your script by exaggerating pitch variations.  

This helps you get a feel for the rhythm so you come out of nature.

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
*Ask good questions*

Questions reflect what you care about. 

Ask questions that you cannot find answers online and important to you. e.g.,

❓ process for creating new courses (imply that you want to bring in something new)
❓ engagement with XYZ Institute (imply your interests in collaboration and building bridges).

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en:
*Express interest*

No matter how impressive your background may be, no one wants to invite candidates for on-campus interviews if they don't show clear interest in the place.

title: How to prepare a phone interview for faculty positions?
en: Best of luck with your interview and hope you find your dream job!!

How to get a tenure-track faculty job?

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
How to get a tenure-track faculty job?

Interested in pursuing an academic career? Summer is the best time to kick off your search!

Here are some tips that I learned. 🧵

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Know the Timeline*

1⃣ Preparation 
• Summer: writing application documents
• Nov-Dec: submit!

2⃣ Phone interview
• Jan-Mar: phone screening, scheduling

3⃣ Onsite interview
• Mar-May: job talk, meet with faculty, offer, negotiation, 2nd visit.

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Invite Yourself*

If you are a superstar, then congrats, you will easily get lots of interviews/offers. But most of us aren't. What can we do? 

💡 Invite yourself to give an invited talk!

• Expand your network.
• Practice your talk and get feedbacks.

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Start before You are Ready*

Yes, it's daunting to present your work to people whom you admire. 😱 You'll never feel that you are ready. 

Do *get started* before you *get ready*. Schedule that talk even if you don't have the slides.

💡 Force yourself to get shxt done *early*!

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Disseminate Your Work Well*

All of your brilliant work cannot reach people if they are behind paywall. 

💡 Make all your papers, code, data easily accessible on your website.

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Prepare for Phone Interviews*

Phone interview questions are structured and predicable (committee will ask the same set of questions to all candidates). 

Prepare to talk about your best work, future paths, how you would get funding, teaching.

💡 Practice, practice, practice!

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Ask Good Questions*

Questions show what you care about, e.g., 

• Work with X center? 👉 Shows your research fits.
• Student recruiting? 👉 Shows what lab you will build. 
• Outreach? 👉 Shows your experiences/plan for DEI efforts.

💡 Self-promotion disguised as questions.

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Give a Good Talk*

A good job talk shows that you are an effective teacher, did excellent research, and know where you are going. 

💡 Convince people OUTSIDE your area! (You already convinced people inside your area, that's why you were invited).

More: https://www.eecs.mit.edu/career-opportunities-at-eecs/faculty-job-talks-tips-from-the-faculty/

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Aim to Communicate, Not to Impress*

In the talk and individual meetings, focusing on communicating what your field is about and why your work is important and interesting. 

💡Avoid trying to impress people with jargon and excessive details.

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
*Thank You Note*

The faculty/student spend 30 mins of their life that they cannot get back meeting with you. 

💡 Show your gratitude and send each of them a thank-you note!

title: How to get a tenure-track faculty job?
en:
Best of luck for your search! 

The whole process is going to be stressful, but at the same time AMAZING experiences! 

Have fun!

How to email faculty as a prospective student?

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
How to email faculty as a prospective student?

Emailing faculty whom you would like to work with is a great way to get you on the radar of the faculty. 

But writing these emails could be daunting 😱 and stressful 😩.

Some tips below 👇

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
*Don't expect a reply*

Here is a rare footage of a faculty during application season.

Faculty are busy. Don't feel disappointed/offended if you don't get a reply.

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
*Check out their website*

Many faculty already indicate if they are looking for new students on their website. 

Asking the same question when you can figure it out in 10 secs may imply that you don't pay attention to details.

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
*Focus on research experience and fit*

Two questions any faculty ask when they review an app:
1⃣ Does this student have the potential to do good research?
2⃣ Can I imagine myself working with this student?

Don't just repeat your GPA/TOEFL/GRE, focus on answering these two Qs.

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
*Get any advice they might offer*

Ask for any advice they may have in your email.
 
Some faculty may offer info like 
• "I am not taking new students this year."
• "Your background may be a good fit for our new faculty XXX. You may contact him/her."

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en:
*Your emails are writing samples*

Write clear, organized, structured emails. 📧

Remember that your emails are writing samples. You may not leave a good impression if you write a sloppy one.

title: How to email faculty as a prospective student?
en: Best of luck with your graduate school application!
How to find a good PhD advisor?

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
How to choose a good Ph.D. advisor?

Grad school application season is coming to an end. Congrats on the offers! Now, how would you choose your advisor that will help you succeed? 

Some tips below (that I wish I knew).

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one that has time for you*

Many faculty don't allocate sufficient time to their students. 

Find an advisor who gives detailed, constructive, honest feedback so you can grow.

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one who is 100% cool for you to take vacation*

You will need it!

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one who sees you as a person*

... and not a brain on a stick.

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find the lab with good peers*

Having great labmates will make your Ph.D. journey so much more enjoyable!

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one that shows, not just tells*

Everyone can tell you that your paper should be clearly rewritten, your ideas should be novel, and your execution should be accurate. 

But HOW? 🤔

Having an advisor that gives concrete examples will accelerate your learning.

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one that supports your research interests*

Doing a Ph.D. is trading money for freedom. 

Find an advisor that cares about your interest, vision, and exploration, not just executing their ideas.

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one that responds to your emails*

Alright, this bar is quite low. 

But I have seen many faculty don't care to help you with the process and only care about your output/results.

title: How to find a good PhD advisor?
en:
*Find one who gets along well with others*

A good advisor helps open up many collaborative opportunities to advance your research!
